subject: Transfer safeguards: onshore cache fallback & audit log retention (proposal)
messages:
From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@carebridgehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: DPA/TIA question re: UK caching fallback and audit logs

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. A couple of risk / legal questions came up in our security review that we need to resolve before we proceed to PO:

1) We need to be confident that EU data can be held in EU regions only, but we also want an option for UK onshore caching in the event of UK latency SLOs (we operate in both jurisdictions). How does Redwood expose an "onshore cache fallback" and how is that limited to transient KV/prefix caching only (i.e., not persistent egress of raw logs)?

2) For the DPA/UK Addendum: what evidence do you typically provide for the TIA/DTIA scope where an onshore cache is used? Specifically, our legal team expects sampling of audit logs, proof of geo-routing, and a subprocessor list with data residency assertions.

Can you point us to a quick checklist and an expected timeline for evidence handoff?

Best,
Emma
Security & Privacy, CareBridge Health

On Behalf of: Tom Avery (Infra)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@carebridgehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Avery <tom.avery@carebridgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA/TIA question re: UK caching fallback and audit logs

Emma / Tom — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front, followed by an internal follow-up with a proposed handoff plan.

1) Onshore cache fallback: Redwood supports policy-based routing where requests from users in the UK can be routed to a UK edge with a short-lived in-memory cache (KV cache, TTL <= 30s by default). Those caches are not persisted to disk; they only hold decryption-ready model context to reduce token latency. We can enforce a config that prevents any disk-backed egress and prevents logs from being exported from the UK edge.

2) Evidence we provide: routing configuration snapshot, a TIA scoping memo (we can produce a DTIA-style summary), a redacted subprocessor inventory with residency assertions, and an audit log sampling export (timeboxed). I attached a high-level DPA summary and a TIA scope request template you can pre-populate.

I will loop in Kimberly and Marissa to scope the TIA (who owns evidence and timelines) and Jonas for the routing/infra confirmation. Expect a proposed evidence handoff plan tomorrow.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_highlevel_v2.pdf, carebridge_tia_scope_request.docx

—Michael
Director, Risk & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 12:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA/TIA question re: UK caching fallback and audit logs

Quick answers:
- Subprocessor list: for pre-signing evidence we can supply a redacted list that includes processor role (e.g., "logging-middleware - US/EU only"), and residency assertions per subprocessor ("operational region: EU; no UK processing unless onshore-fallback enabled"). Legal prefers redaction of contact emails and contract rates.
- Residency assertion: we can provide a signed statement on company letterhead confirming residency boundaries and contractual limits tied to the UK Addendum. That is standard.
- Acceptable redaction level: redaction of commercial terms and emails; retain service names, operational regions, and control summaries.

I recommend we prepare: 1) redacted subprocessor inventory PDF, 2) signed residency assertion, 3) routing config snapshot, 4) 7-day audit sample (redacted PII). I can own the doc sign-off for the residency assertion.

—Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Privacy

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 07:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA/TIA question re: UK caching fallback and audit logs

Thanks — timeline estimate and operational notes below. Planned work:
- Audit log sample (7 days): we can generate a timeboxed export (JSONL) and apply field-level redaction rules to remove sensitive user payloads. Estimated lead time: 2 business days once scope confirmed.
- Routing config snapshot: we can freeze and export current routing policy and CBOR config for a specific date/time. Lead time: same day (ops can snapshot).
- Onshore cache behavior: default is in-memory; persistence toggle is gated behind infra change and requires DCO approval. We can provide a config that forces TTL <= 30s and disables disk spill.
- Evidence packaging: ops will stage items in a protected Drive folder and share a time-limited link (I can coordinate).

Action items for Michael: confirm exact date range for audit sample (they asked for a 7-day window; propose last business week).
Action items for Kimberly: once redaction level is final, we'll run the export and hand it to you to sign residency assertion.

I'll plan a 3-business-day handoff from confirmation to evidence delivery if we get sign-off today.

—Marissa
Senior Manager, Customer Ops
